material.learn: Different kinds of support at one price (a swing low, an average, a retracement) make a stronger floor than any one alone.

material.head: Retesting its breakout level
material.text: It broke out above the February high and has come back to test it from above: old resistance acting as new support.
material.learn: After a breakout, price often comes back to the line it broke; old resistance becomes new support.

material.head: Next support −3.4% below
material.text: The next floor under it is −3.4% below (1.4 ATR), where 4 levels (3 kinds) meet: the April breakout level, the 61.8% retracement of the Mar 9–Jul 29 rise and the 20-day average.
material.learn: A price where buyers stepped in before.

material.head: Selling is losing force
material.text: A lower low in price (Oct 14) against a higher low in momentum (4 of 7 gauges): regular bullish divergence.
material.learn: Lower price lows with rising momentum lows: sellers are tiring.

against.head: Downtrend on every average
against.text: Price is below its falling 50-day and 200-day averages, and the 50-day is below the 200-day.
against.learn: Both averages falling with price under them: the long trend points down.

against.head: Weekly chart: declining
against.text: Price is below a falling 30-week average: the declining stage.
against.learn: Stocks cycle through basing, advancing, topping and declining; longs pay in the advancing stage.

against.head: A lower high and a lower low
against.text: Its last swing high and swing low each came in under the one before.
against.learn: Falling swing highs and lows are the steps of a downtrend.

material.text: Such signals lagged the market in the desk's study.

material.head: Holding its rising 20-day
material.text: It dipped to its rising 20-day average in the last three sessions and held above it.
material.learn: The average close of the last 20, 50 or 200 sessions; rising averages mark uptrends and often act as support.
